app.title: Ghosted
app.subtitle: Find out who doesn't follow you back on Instagram
app.disclaimer: Your credentials are used only for this session and are never written to disk. Using this tool may violate Instagram's Terms of Service; use it at your own discretion and in moderation.
about.header: ℹ️ What is this and how do I use it?
about.purpose: **Purpose:** Ghosted is an educational project. It exists to show, hands-on, how a real automation against an undocumented private API actually works (2FA quirks, device fingerprinting, rate-limiting) and how to handle sessions/credentials with reasonable security practices. It isn't meant as a product for mass or recurring use.
about.what_it_does: **What it does:** compares who you follow on Instagram against who follows you back, and shows the difference — accounts you follow that don't follow you. From there you can filter them, export them, or unfollow the ones you pick, with pauses between actions so it doesn't look like a bot.
about.how_to_use:
**How to use it:**
1. Log in by pasting a session cookie (see below for how to export one).
2. Tap "Scan followers" and wait for it to finish.
3. Review the results: search, filter, mark accounts to ignore (whitelist) or to unfollow.
4. If you're unfollowing accounts, confirm and wait — the pauses are intentional, don't rush them.
about.credentials_warning: **About your password and the session cookie:** both are, in practice, a full key to your Instagram account. Never share either, or paste them into sites you don't trust — not even educational tools like this one. If you use cookie login, delete it from wherever you exported it as soon as you're done, and consider logging out that session from Instagram's own security settings. This app only keeps them in memory during your browser session and never writes them to disk, but that doesn't protect you from pasting them in the wrong place yourself.
login.cookie.help: Skips 2FA entirely by reusing a session your browser already has. Log into instagram.com normally, then use a cookie-export extension (e.g. EditThisCookie, Cookie-Editor) on that tab to export the cookies for instagram.com, and paste the result below - you don't need to find or edit anything inside it, the app looks for the piece it needs on its own.
login.cookie.danger: ⚠️ That exported value is a live key to your account, equivalent to your password — anyone who has it can act as you on Instagram without ever entering a code. Never paste it anywhere you don't fully trust, and once you're done with this tool, delete it from wherever you exported it to (and consider logging out that browser session from Instagram's own security settings, which invalidates it).
login.cookie.howto_header: 📋 How to export the cookie with EditThisCookie (step by step)
login.cookie.howto_intro: We're spelling this out on purpose: we want you to see with your own eyes how easy it is to copy full access to an account when someone has three minutes and the right cookie. It's exactly the same ease - and the same risk - as any other account of yours (bank, email, social media) if you leave a session open on a machine you don't control.
login.cookie.howto_install: **1. Install the extension** (one time only): install [EditThisCookie v3](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/editthiscookie-v3/ojfebgpkimhlhcblbalbfjblapadhbol) from the Chrome Web Store ("Cookie-Editor" works the same way too, if you prefer that one). Any extension like this asks for permission to read the cookies of sites you visit - that's literally what you're about to use in your favor, so only install the official version from a verified developer, never a copy from a random link.
login.cookie.howto_export: **2. Export the cookie:** log into instagram.com normally in that same tab. With the Instagram tab active, click the extension's icon → export button (an export/outward-arrow icon, usually says "Export" or copy as JSON) → this automatically copies all of the site's cookies to your clipboard.
login.cookie.howto_paste: **3. Paste it here:** come back to this Ghosted tab and paste (Ctrl/Cmd+V) into the field above. That's it - in under a minute, without ever touching your password or a code, anyone with physical or remote access to your Chrome session could have done exactly the same thing.
login.cookie.howto_after: **4. After using it:** clear what you copied from your clipboard (paste it once somewhere harmless, like the address bar, then delete it - so it isn't sitting there for the next accidental Ctrl+V). If you exported it to a file, delete that file. Don't save it in notes, a chat, or anywhere else in plain text.
login.cookie.machine_header: 🔒 How to protect your machine so this doesn't happen to you without you knowing
login.cookie.machine_tips:
- **Encrypt your disk** (FileVault on Mac, BitLocker on Windows) - if someone steals your machine while it's off, without this they can read everything, cookies included.
- **Lock your session** whenever you step away, always. An unattended, logged-in Chrome session is exactly the scenario you just simulated.
- **Only install extensions from verified sources** and check what permissions they ask for - a malicious extension can export your cookies without you clicking anything, in the background, for any site you visit.
- **Keep your OS and browser updated** - most cookie-stealing malware ("infostealers") exploits vulnerabilities that are already patched in newer versions.
- **Be wary of clipboard managers that sync to the cloud** - if you copied a cookie, that value may have been replicated to another device of yours without you noticing.
- **Actually log out** when you're done on an important site, don't just close the tab - many session cookies stay valid until they expire on their own or you explicitly revoke them.
login.cookie.label: Paste the exported cookies (or just the sessionid value)
login.cookie.error.not_found: Couldn't find a "sessionid" cookie in what you pasted. Make sure you exported the cookies for instagram.com while logged in.
login.cookie.error.invalid: That session looks invalid or expired. Export the cookies again from a fresh instagram.com tab.
